{"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"A local agent works against a remote reflow2 server, named by URL, exactly as it does against a local one","priority":"high","provenance":"authored","source":"Anthony (who:ajs), dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-25; raised with flo2's api.flo2.io and a family member's workplace in mind","statement":"A person shall be able to start reflow2 on their own machine as a local client of a remote reflow2 server named by URL: flo2's api.flo2.io, or an organization's own shared server. Their agent (Claude Code, Grok Build, any MCP client) talks to it over stdio exactly as it talks to a local reflow2, and cannot tell the difference.

IN ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-09-25: "a small client that gets installed locally that acts at the intermediary between flo2.io reflow2 mcp and the local claude code CLI or grok build? The agent then talks to the intermediary and knows no difference of whether it is talking to the local reflow2 mcp or the remote/centrally hosted mcp" — and, on choosing it: "my brother has discussed having their own shared reflow2 mcp at work that everybody has access to, so option c would support that, it would just be pointing it some local url_to_shared_reflow2_server.organization.org ... instead of pointing it to api.flo2.io".

WHAT "KNOWS NO DIFFERENCE" HAS TO COVER:
1. THE CREDENTIAL, AND NO ONE WAY OF GETTING IT IS HARDCODED. Anthony, 2026-09-25: "we don't hardcode option (a) as how everybody will have to access their remote mcp server". The client supports whatever the server's operator chooses:
   - NONE, for a server reached over a private network or VPN;
   - A KEY OR TOKEN THE PERSON SUPPLIES, however their organization issues it, read from an environment variable, a file or the OS keychain, and sent as a header;
   - A SIGN-IN FLOW (browser or device code) for a server that offers one.
   Whichever it is, the client keeps it out of the agent's environment where it can. Choosing among them is the server operator's policy, not reflow2's. flo2 chooses sign-in for api.flo2.io because of its own req:no-user-api-keys; an organization's shared server may hand out keys. reflow2 itself still authenticates nothing (dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id).
2. WHO A WRITE IS FOR. On a stateless server the only way to say it is per request, so the client carries `_meta["reflow2/writes_for"]` on every call it forwards (the writes_for tool, v0.71.0). A shared credential says which client, never which person.
3. THE FILES. A remote server would save the design export and measure artifact files on its own disk. The client runs on the person's machine, so it can write the export into the local working tree and measure local files, sending their checksums as asserted. Without this, the agent can tell the difference the first time it exports or reconciles.

ALREADY HALF-BUILT: `--shared` is a stdio client that forwards to a `--serve-shared` HTTP daemon on loopback. This is that client, pointed at a remote address and carrying a credential.

ORDER, set by Anthony 2026-09-25: flo2's direct sign-in (option a, flo2's cap:mcp-endpoint) first, then this.","status":"proposed"}
